The aphorism is most often misunderstood by being taken literally, as if Maine claimed that status-based relations had vanished and all modern law rests on contract. He was describing a long-run tendency in which the family-based, ascribed basis of rights and duties gave way to voluntary agreement between individuals, and he acknowledged that status-like ties persisted. Some readings also misrepresent his concept of status, but the literal reading is the more common error.

CONFIDENCE: 68
